findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on invalid file path or unreadable file
findings.failure_mode: Any filesystem error (missing file, permissions, ENOENT) causes a panic instead of returning a typed error, violating the zero-unwrap rule
findings.fix: Return a Result type. Use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| ...)? or match on Err and propagate as a domain error.

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked indexed access on a Vec without bounds checking
findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than one comma-producing field will panic with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to extract the first field safely, or use .get(0) with proper error handling.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() uses both unchecked indexing and unwrap on fallible parse
findings.failure_mode: Index out of bounds if line has only one field; parse failure on non-numeric input both cause panic instead of typed error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get name and remainder, then parse remainder with .map_err() to return a typed ParseError.

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy cast from u32 that silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value in range 65536..u32::MAX is silently truncated to u16, producing an incorrect Record without any error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(...) to produce a typed overflow error, or use checked_cast with domain error.

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() then indexed access into parts Vec instead of split_once
findings.failure_mode: Allocates a full Vec of all split parts, iterates every field, and then only uses indices 0 and 1 — wasteful allocation and violates the split_once rule
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to split into exactly two parts. Parse the second part directly. No intermediate Vec allocation needed.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side-effecting log call inside a data-parsing function
findings.failure_mode: Mixes I/O side effects with data parsing, making the function non-deterministic and impossible to test in isolation without capturing stdout
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing pipeline. If observability is needed, return a side-channel result or push logging to the imperative shell layer that calls this function.

findings.problem: Function signature returns Vec<Record> with no error type — all failures silently panic
findings.failure_mode: No caller can distinguish between EOF, parse error, overflow, or filesystem error — all produce panics rather than recoverable errors
findings.fix: Change return type to Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError> or Result<Record, RecordError> for the iterator item, and define a domain error enum.

findings.problem: Record value field is u16 but parsing goes through u32 without validation — illegal u16 values are unreachable but the construction path is unchecked
findings.failure_mode: The value field should only ever hold valid u16 values, but the only construction path (parse + as cast) can silently truncate without the compiler enforcing the invariant
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from in the parse path so that out-of-range values are caught at construction time and returned as errors.

findings.problem: Record name is String — empty string is a legal but likely invalid state for a record name
findings.failure_mode: A Record with an empty name is constructable and cannot be distinguished from a valid named record without runtime checks
findings.fix: Introduce a Name newtype with a fallible constructor that rejects empty strings, making empty names unrepresentable at the type level.
